questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That Spanish is the national language in the country of destination. In this way I was able to practice the language, both for personal reasons and for future career possibilities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I enjoy more the way of studying in the University of Copenhagen, therefore not 10. It

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy to find the necessary information as both the host university and my home university send various e-mails with information e.g. about how to get to the university in Mexico, how to change a course or when and where exchange-meetings would be held.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received written help via the host university's mail system, orally in the internacional office on campus as well as advice from other students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy, as I had a friend but me in contact with a Danish student who had studied abroad at the same university in Mexico. Therefore, I wrote that student who gave me recommendations about housing off-campus. I lived in a student housing called Casa Roja, which I can recommend. There is space for around 14 students with two kitchens and separate bathrooms. It is located approximately 2 km. from the university - perfect if one likes a little morning walk.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I recommend living off-campus as it e.g. gives the student a possibility to more easily explore different parts of the town. It is a way of living that can be highly social, so if one prefers a larger amount of private space, it may not be the best option. But for me it was a great way to get to know people from the moment I arrived, creating a safe space with other exchange students for whom studying abroad equally is a new experience. In short, it is a great possibility to make friends.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: To gain 30 ECTS points I had to choose five courses. Initially it was a bit difficult finding all the necessary information about what courses was available during the spring semester. After choosing some courses and getting them accepted by the host university, one of the courses I had chosen was declined by my home university with the explanation that the course did not qualify as bachelor level. Therefore, I had to change one course. I wanted to change to a course taught in Spanish, but as I did not have a high enough score in the language test, initially it was not possible to take courses in Spanish. After talking with the internacional office at the host university, and changing courses twice I was allowed to change to a course taught in Spanish.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Oral (inn person and via telephone) and written.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was successful as I got help from the international office at the host university changing some courses after the deadline of registration.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do it within the deadline and if you are in doubt about something rather ask the host university twice. The people working at the internacional office are really helpful and want to make things work for the students.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had five courses, the level of some of the courses was fairly high. For instance the course of philosophy was fairly difficult. Two of my courses were on the other hand fairly easy academically, in the way that we did not go into depths with the material of the course. With that said I would still say that I have learned new things; in some cases more superficially.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was quite a different fro the way of teaching at UCPH. I some ways it felt more as if being in high school in the way that you would get points for making your home work or coming to class. The students had more home work than at UCPH that you had to hand in every weak for the teacher to see that the students were participating in the course. At UCPH the students, at a higher degree, have the responsibility for their own attendance and how much they learn.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Humanistic thought (philosophy)
Communication and Globalisation 
Bilinguisme 
Translation Practices 
Introduction to Translation

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the two courses regarding translation, as the teacher was structured and held interesting clases. Furthermore, it is interesting if one is interested in the field of translation and linguistics.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Going on trips to visit different places in Mexico.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was less expensive than in Denmark. In general it was cheaper to live in Mexico than in Denmark. Some cafes in the host town in Mexico had prices comparable to Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Different celebrations such as internacional women's day, valentines day, sports installations such as a gym, a swimming pool, or football fields, different on-campus food markets, a library, seminars and cultural events such as art exhibitions or theater shows (though I did not attend the latter).

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Swimming in the pool, go to art exhibitions or fairs in the center of the university. Outside of campus explore small cafés, join a sports team, go to Climbing Club ´Moonrock Boulders´, by groceries and the mercado central. These are ways of engaging in the life of the town, maybe feeling more at home and finding hidden gems.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore Cholula and Puebla, visit other regions of Mexico.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Overall it was fairly easy to adjust to the culture. As there where many exchange students in the town I lived, the culture was also affected by the presence of foreigners. Furthermore, local students where happy to help explain how something works, e.g. how to buy a sim card for your phone, which stores have the best prices or if some parts of the town are unsafe to walk in.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Initiate conversations during or after clases, maybe asking for students´ contact information or asking if they would be interested drinking a coffee with you one day or if they can help you with practical information. My experience is that the local students are open and want to help and socialise.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Machisme

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people in Mexico are in general all quite open and helpful, also towards strangers. I really enjoyed the food as well. There are colours everywhere.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Do not stress, people are helpful and will aid if you have any doubts about anything. 
- The way of studying and teaching is different from that of Copenhagen University. Of course this depends on the courses, but you might have a lot of homework all the time.
- The teachers are open to help you if you want to move a deadline or have any doubts about anything.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
If you are living off-campus it might be nice to rent or buy a bike to get around the town faster and easier. There is a facebook page called something like ´venta y renta en UDLAP´ where students at the university sell used things. Here one might find things that one needs less expensive e.g. books, a bike, clothes, blankets etc. 

Even though you get recommended not walking alone at night, I did not feel unsafe walking alone at dark. The only thing is that you have to be vary of the street dogs. The dogs might be a bit aggressive at night, but during the day they do no harm.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from around the world, both local Mexicans and other exchange students was very rewarding and gave me other points of view of the world. Furthermore, understanding how the everyday life works in the town, and learning more Spanish was rewarding.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: balance school work with activities in my spare time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
